utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If any party did --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I withdraw that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: One last question, sir: You stated that the sources of water in Bascarsija and Jagomir were controlled by the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I can't remember the name of the source above Bascarsija towards Vucja Luka, that source was under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So in order to distribute water to any area, essentially, electricity is needed, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So in the absence of electricity the water source, the source of water, does not help, does it, in order to distribute it to any area?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: Water pumps at the source couldn't work.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So, therefore, you do agree with me that in the absence of electricity, water cannot be distributed?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any need to re-examine the witness, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radojevic, Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I am looking for just for clarification. From where the Reljevo substation got -- did the Reljevo station get the power supply?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: I have already said that the Reljevo substation received electricity from Kakanj Jablanica, power from those directions. And from Visegrad through the Vogosca transformer station, via 110 watt power line which goes through Kota and Zuc. It would receive power from that power line. Those are the two directions from which it received power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: You said that --

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: And if the Trial Chamber has nothing against this, I have other details that I can provide with regard to the power line poles which were destroyed in the eastern part in order to make the power station malfunction, and to cut off the electricity in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No, I am sorry --

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: In both parts of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Not at this very moment. You said that if you switched off the power of -- at the Buca Potok or Reljevo, the city would suffer a blackout; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: If you cut it off in Reljevo, the entire town would be without electricity, both the Serbian part of town and the part of the town that was under the control of the BH Army. But once again, I will repeat this: This never happened, apart from when there was damage inflicted on the power line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: So that included both sides of the city, the Serbian and the Bosnian parts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. When the Serbian part of the town had electricity, the Bosnian part -- the Bosniak part also had electricity. Only if we didn't have time to carry out repairs on the power line which went through Zuc, but if we refused to do that, they would simply cut the electricity supply off in Kakanj and no one would have electricity. So we depended on each other. We had to carry out the repairs as quickly as possible so that both parts of the town could have electricity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radojevic, Judge El Mahdi also has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, there is one matter that I would like to clarify. Did the Reljevo station at the moment, at a given moment in time during the September 1992 to August 1994 period, was this station -- was this station damaged during that period?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact time or the date. It was shelled. And on that occasion, an on-duty electrician that was working there, he is wounded, and I think he has remained disable. I don't know which leg he was wounded in. There was a minor malfunction, but it was quickly repaired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And do you think that this was a premeditated attack? Was this station targeted or was this station near to some other military target?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: My personal opinion is that it was shelled intentionally because the Blazuj power station -- the transformer station was also fired at from the direction of Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radojevic, I also have a question for you. You've told us extensively on how damage to pylons would interrupt the power line between Reljevo and Buca Potok. Are you aware of any other reasons why it ever happened that the power supply from Reljevo to Buca Potok was interrupted? So, apart from damage to pylons.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't know of any other occasions because I personally, I was personally in charge of the repairs and the maintenance of the power lines in the area that I mentioned at the beginning when questions were put to me by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that for a longer period of time you would have no electricity in Ilidza, for example, without you being sent to repair the power lines?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: I think that at one time the period when Sarajevo had no electricity for three months, I think that that happened. But no one could have sent me out to carry out repairs. If I wasn't able to go to the site, those malfunctions occurred at the places that I have already mentioned. We tried to go and carry out repairs on the power line. But since it wasn't possible to reach agreement -- when we could reach an agreement, when we went out with a team, when I went out with a team, I can't remember when, Ekrem Bicakcic contacted me personally via radio. He contacted me and he asked me -- he used my nickname, he said, "Veljo, what do we have to do today, what do we have to do to the power lines?" I said "Mr. Bicakcic, as long as there is no shooting from your side from Reljevo to Poljin above Vogosca, that's all you have to do and my team and Sabanovic Muhrem, who was popularly called Saban, we'll do everything else. That does not concern you."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know exactly where at that moment the damage occurred that you could not repair for three months? Do you know the exact location of the damage?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is in the Reljevo, Vogosca, Buca Potok, part of the power line from the elevation from what they called Jezevo at the time to Golo Brdo and onwards in the direction of Zabrdje. I can't be more precise. I could show you where that was at the site, but I can't explain this in words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that you are referring to part of a line. How precise is your knowledge as to the specific spot where the damage was?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that part very well because those sites where there were malfunctions, a kilometre or so, I went there at least 100, 150 times in the course of the war, if not, even more often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us at what distance this was from the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR RADOJEVIC
utterances.text: The Vogosca-Reljevo power line ran along the entire length between the demarcation lines. And the Reljevo-Buca Potok power line cut through the demarcation lines. And at that part, the lines of both the armies were between 100 and 150 metres, at the most, in the Golo Brdo area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answers. Is there any -- Mr. Radojevic, since the -- since you have answered all the questions of the parties and of the Bench, I would like to thank you very much for coming and testifying even if it was at a long distance from The Hague. And I know that your journey back home is not as far as for most of the witnesses, but I hope that you will be safe home again soon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I really wanted to appear in The Hague, but as I am ill at the moment, this is why I am not in the same courtroom with you and this is why I am speaking to you in this manner and this is why I was not able to appear in person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is what I had to say in response to the questions asked of me about the power line poles which had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all I wasn't able to say. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's addition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, and I am addressing now both the representatives of Sarajevo and here in the Hague that this concludes the videolink testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the same is true for Sarajevo. I take it there is nothing that should be brought to the attention of the Chamber at this very moment by the representative of the Registry in Sarajevo. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: THE REGISTRAR IN SARAJEVO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The technicians may close the transmission channel to Sarajevo. At least the Chamber doesn't need it any more. I was informed that the witness that started his testimony yesterday is not available at this very moment, which surprises me. But I also was informed that he was asked at least to be there not later than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is a bit surprising because I asked yesterday, although it might not be today, that the witness should make himself available. I asked the Victims and Witnesses Unit to trace him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I informed the section during the break that they should contact the witness who should be appearing today. Perhaps we should have a break to check whether he will be appearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before having a break, we could deal with a few other issues. Yes, perhaps first we should give a decision on the admission into evidence of the document or rather the videotape played during the testimony of Mr. Radojevic. Madam Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D348/8, is the video; and D348/8.A is the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That video is then admitted into evidence, and the transcript as well. Then I -- Mr. Ierace, yesterday you objected against the question of Ms. Pilipovic, you certainly remember that, about warehouses where the Territorial Defence was and the army was. It has been checked yesterday afternoon. In the initial answer of the witness, he mentioned the Territorial Defence. So when Ms. Pilipovic continued with her next question to mention that, she was perfectly right to do so. But it did not appear on our transcript. But it has been checked by now. Then I promised the parties that I would give guidance in a few respects relatively soon. I will give you some guidance on some issues that have been raised during the last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has discussed many issues that came up during the recent weeks, and I will try to give you, in a comprehensive way, some guidance in respect of these issues. First of all, the list of witnesses. The list of witnesses, the form prescribed by the Chamber when the Prosecution was presenting its case applies without any restriction to the Defence. Witnesses should be listed when an update of the list of witnesses is given always in the running order so that we start with the witness that is testifying at that very moment. Not later than seven days prior to the testimony given, the exhibits to be used should be known to the other party. If a document is not yet listed and the need to confront the witness with such a document comes up which may occur, upon good cause shown why it was not previously mentioned in the list, the document may be used. If that is a new document, a document not yet known to the other party which of course -- which, for example, is possible if the witness brings unexpectedly a certain document, then extra time may be granted to the other party and that will bring a stay of the proceedings, usually the Prosecution. So extra time may be granted to prepare for cross-examination in respect of that document. If the document is not new, but already known prior to the testimony of the witness but perhaps not seven days in advance, then the list should be updated with priority as soon as the Defence knows that a document will be used not yet in the list and already disclosed or known to the Prosecution, the list should be updated immediately. When during the testimony of a witness reference is made to earlier testimony, either of that same witness or of another witness, the following applies: If the part quoted that same day, page and line should be indicated unless it is immediately proceeding the new question. So if it is just two or three questions ago, it is not necessary to indicate page and line. If, however, there is more space between the question and the testimony to which reference is made, then page and line should be mentioned. If it is of a previous day, the quoting of this testimony should be done literally. So not a vague reference, but literal wordings of what has been said. Objections are not, as a rule, an opening of argument. The type of objection should be clearly mentioned such as relevance or misrepresentation of earlier testimony, and as a rule, the objection should not take more than two lines. Objections should not contain comments and should not lead the witness. Then the issue of the witness summaries. Updates of the witness summaries should always contain a reference to the earlier summaries or the earlier sources on which it -- to which it adds. The main purpose of the 65 ter summaries is to give a summary of the facts that enables the other party to prepare for cross-examination. If, therefore, as we experienced several times, specific questions will be put in respect of certain parts of the confrontation line, it should be clear what parts of that confrontation line, and if relevant facts are mentioned in respect of sniping or shelling incidents, it should be clear to which incidents these relevant facts pertain and what is the kind of facts. Since we have experienced now that, for example, lines of sight are usually dealt with in examination-in-chief, it may be apparent to the Prosecution that this is usually a relevant issue, and it is therefore not necessary to specifically mention that. The same would be true for combat activity in the area. The Chamber understands that relevant facts in respect of certain incidents would comprise these usually covered issues, although in the beginning when that was not yet cleared, it should have mentioned that it was about the lines of sight. But if there are other facts, other specific facts for such incidents, they should be mentioned. And it is about issues rather than about every single fact that will come up in answers. To give you an example, yesterday facts were asked to the witness as to the impact of mortar shells on hard or soft soil. Not every single answer the witness would give in that area would need to be mentioned in the summary, but this is an issue which was not clear from the summary given, and a very generic reference to weapons and the use of weapons were not sufficient under these circumstances. If there are specific areas the Defence decides not to cover, although they are mentioned in the summary, then it's fair to inform the Prosecution that that area will not be the subject of examination-in-chief any more. That does not mean that every question that will not be put to the witness should be mentioned to the Prosecution, but that if an area, if a certain issue will not be touched upon during the examination-in-chief, that the Defence fairly should inform the Prosecution about that. Then the last issue is that when the Defence has not put to Prosecution witnesses any element of what during the examination of the Defence witnesses seems to be part of its case, the Chamber will not prohibit those questions, but will consider any objection, and it might eventually result in procedural remedies. One of them might be, depending on the circumstances, recall of witnesses at a later stage. These were the issues I would like to give the parties some guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has not been found yet. Have you been in touch yesterday with the Victims and Witnesses Unit, Ms. Pilipovic, to the availability of the witness today? I am asking -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And during the break I also asked for this to be confirmed, since I had been told that I wouldn't have a videolink because in my planning, I was planning another witness for the videolink from 12.00 onwards. Since I knew that the witness hadn't accepted this, I asked for the witness to be ready as of 12.00, the witness who started giving his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the content of your communication with the Victims and Witnesses Unit yesterday about availability of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't personally have contact with them, but through my colleague who always contacts the Victims and Witnesses Unit, I asked them to inform us that the witness should be here today, so that the witness could testify, since I knew that I wouldn't have a witness for the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have been in touch with the Victims and Witnesses Unit yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I asked Ms. Pilipovic to do that. When she says "her colleague" she is referring to the person whom you have occasionally seen here, who usually assists us who is in Belgrade, who called us from Belgrade, I think. But I haven't been in contact but we took care to take measures for this witness to appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you instructed the Victims and Witnesses Unit -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you have -- the Victims and Witnesses Unit has been instructed yesterday to make the witness available also today?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's what I informed my colleague of after my colleague informed me that the witness for the videolink was supposed to testified today at 12.00. I was informed that the witness decided not to testify. And during the break at 10.20 at I again asked the Victims and Witnesses Unit to be contacted so as to ensure the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber will try to obtain information of the Victims and Witnesses Unit why the witness is not available at this very moment. We will adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before we -- just before we adjourn, might I give the Trial Chamber some information in closed session. It will only take a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do you have anything to address in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, only two things, though. The usual problem that concerns translation, that's the first thing, and the second thing I wanted to say something about or rather as a follow-up with regard to the order that you have just issued. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that can be dealt with in open session. I would rather leave the translation issue until the very last moment because there might come up new ones. Please tell us what you would like to tell us in respect of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The Defence took note of your recent order, and we thank you for it. We simply wanted to point out two matters. Experience teaches us very often, given the time we have to restrict ourselves for the examination of a witness, we don't often know whether we will be able to cover all the subjects. During the course of the examination, certain choices have to be made, and in the course of the examination one decides not to raise certain issues, for example, the map was a particular example with regard to the previous witness. We don't know about these things in advance. This depends on how possible it is for the witness to respond quickly and how possible it is of the parties not to interrupt the proceedings. So it is not possible to respect this literally. And the second point with regard to this issue, and Mr. President is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may respond to that immediately. The Chamber is aware and, therefore, I think you could completely obey to the order, because what I said is that if it becomes clear prior to the testimony that certain subjects will not be covered, that you should then inform the Prosecution. The Chamber is aware that in the course of the examination, a development might occur such that you, because of the relevance or whatever other reasons such as time, that you cannot touch upon certain subjects. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The second matter which is a little more upsetting for us that I wanted to raise is that during the Prosecution case we received very frequently statements, witness statements that were very long, going in great detail, while in a matter of fact, it turned out that these witnesses suddenly were not speaking about a lot of the things that we were told about, were informed about. So I don't think the Prosecution was in the same situation to tell us this witness will not be speaking about this or that. So I believe that there is a lack of balance between the parties and I thank you for making observations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think -- I am not quite sure whether I earlier paid attention to it. Of course the Chamber has also considered this. The Prosecution is under an obligation to provide the Defence with statements, and in that respect, the obligations of the Prosecution go further than the obligations of the Defence. So it is not obliged to provide witness statements. The Prosecution also has provided summaries of the testimony of witnesses which are not the same as the statements. So in general terms, the Defence could have oriented itself primarily on the summaries and find the details of those subjects covered by the summaries in the statements of the witness in respect of those subjects. So the Chamber is aware of the difference in position with perhaps advantages and disadvantages between the parties. Then, Mr. Ierace, you wanted to address the Chamber in closed session. For one minute we turn into closed session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I promised you that and please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very quickly, line 320 in the English transcript, something was not translated regarding to the Blazuj group, page 4, line 15 in the French transcript, it wasn't said that the witness went into the mountains, maintained which was a mountain. Also there was another person that was mentioned, I think Huso Habanovic. His name we will not find in the English transcript. On page 10 Defence were given by the population that was residing near the Zrak factory. That is not in the English transcript. And also another thing is that he went out to do reparations, to repair. That is not in the English transcript. I believe that the man that he went to do the repairs with, I believe his last name is Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. We will then adjourn for 25 minutes so that it is up to 20 minutes to 1.00, but the parties may try to get information on whether the witness is available or not because the Chamber is informed that there is no other witness available. So we could not continue, but let's try to do our utmost best to get the witness into the courtroom in 25 minutes. Perhaps it comes close to lunchtime that could perhaps solve the problem. We will adjourn until 20 minutes to 1.00, and if the witness is not available, we will continue tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of November 2002 at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
